answer: When an AI agent joins the PoA economy it must stake a cryptographic deposit into a vault and submit a signed sonnet‑style proof of work that references the current horizon block hash. The network then rate‑limits reward vesting, releasing tokens only after a linear schedule that spans many epochs, so a farm of freshly minted identities accrues value at a fraction of the cost of its upfront stake. An attacker therefore pays the full deposit for each fake identity while receiving negligible earnings, making a Sybil attack economically infeasible.
